entries.title: Smoother first-time setup
entries.summary: The setup command no longer stops for npx's install prompt, Codex keeps your per-tool approval settings when it reconnects, Engram's hooks carry readable labels, and setups made earlier for single folders can be switched to the new connection in one answer.

entries.title: Connect a computer in one step
entries.summary: Run `npx @ani-hq/engram-mcp@latest`, approve in your browser, and Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, including their desktop apps, are connected with their own keys. Engram then works in every repo, with no config or Markdown files to edit.

entries.title: Release record and Cursor results
entries.summary: Records the 28 October release and the live Cursor transfer runs: 6 of 9 pass, and Cursor-first interruption is not yet verified.

entries.title: A public changelog
entries.summary: This page: every change to Engram, newest first, with the time it landed and a link to its source.

entries.title: Bridge 0.6.0 with task checkpoints
entries.summary: The `@ani-hq/engram-mcp` bridge moves to 0.6.0 with the checkpoint command and continuation hooks. Live transfer results across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor are recorded in the continuation spec.

entries.title: Cookieless site analytics
entries.summary: Public pages count views, a few named calls to action and sign-up sources with a first-party script. No cookies, IP addresses, user agents or emails are stored, and Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

entries.title: Task handoffs between agents
entries.summary: Agents can save a compact task record: objective, plan, decisions, blockers and next step. Another agent, or the same one after a crash or usage limit, can find it and continue from the last confirmed save. Activity gains a Handoffs view with a copyable continue prompt.

entries.title: Sharing in team workspaces
entries.summary: Team owners and members can browse the approved excerpts they received, open team memory, and switch to a personal workspace to prepare a new share.

entries.title: Compact action buttons
entries.summary: Buttons share one compact 32px size on desktop across the interface. Touch screens and narrow widths keep 44px targets.

entries.title: A complete agent connection prompt
entries.summary: Connections offers a full setup prompt to paste into an agent, with the endpoint and intended workspace. It uses native MCP setup where available and exact guidance otherwise.

entries.title: Simpler agent connections
entries.summary: Connect an agent shows the shared MCP endpoint right away. Access keys and agent-specific help are optional steps.

entries.title: Focused Connections, checks in Activity
entries.summary: Connections lists your agents and opens a dedicated setup dialog for each one, and reconnecting keeps existing settings. Workspace checks moved into Activity.

entries.title: Reliable memory save confirmations
entries.summary: Explicit memory saves get a longer, bounded deadline, so a slow write that reached the server is no longer reported as unavailable. Animation playback controls were removed.

entries.title: Useful memory at small budgets
entries.summary: Installed agent guidance is shorter, so a 1 KiB retrieval budget still leaves room for useful context. Grok setup steps match its current connector flow.

entries.title: Guided memory setup and repair
entries.summary: One guided command from Connections installs or repairs the memory workflow, without editing Markdown or configuration files. File changes are checked first and rolled back on failure.

entries.title: Reliable, bounded agent memory
entries.summary: Retrieval is task-aware and capped so it does not flood an agent's context. Adds native runtime adapters, portable guidance, and JavaScript and Python SDKs.

entries.title: Connection lifecycle and profile photos
entries.summary: Owners can archive, restore or delete connections without losing saved work, and upload, replace or remove a profile photo. Public profiles get quieter activity cards.

entries.title: Calmer handoff diagram on mobile
entries.summary: The landing-page handoff diagram is quieter and fits short screens, with compact agent cards on mobile.

entries.title: Shared controls and animated handoffs
entries.summary: The landing page explains scoped sharing with a looping save-and-recall illustration and shows 21 agent products with locally bundled logos. Motion pauses offscreen.

entries.title: New interface system and profile layouts
entries.summary: One graphite and mint design system now covers the app, public pages, email and social cards. Public profiles offer two layouts, Living studio and Field notes, with up to three written highlights.

entries.title: Stricter release smoke checks
entries.summary: Before issuing a temporary read credential, the release check verifies the exact candidate revision, image digest and provider-free worker configuration.

entries.title: Reviewed selective sharing
entries.summary: Describe which context belongs with a team or another agent, preview bounded excerpts, and approve the exact text. Shares are fixed snapshots, so new source text needs a fresh review.

entries.title: Clearer beta pricing
entries.summary: Hosted beta pricing shows 60 days free with an invite instead of $0, and says access starts after email verification. The site states the plan to sponsor open-source projects from revenue.

entries.title: Fix worker preparation retries
entries.summary: Re-running mail or billing worker preparation updates existing schedules correctly, without enabling delivery or billing.

entries.title: Separate connection for operator setup
entries.summary: Operator bootstrap and maintenance use a scoped provisioner connection instead of the restricted request pool.

entries.title: Fix scheduled worker configuration
entries.summary: Mail and Jev billing jobs get the correct Cloud Run execution settings and database attachment.

entries.title: Explicit operator workspace for Jev
entries.summary: The operator's default Jev workspace is named explicitly, alongside the exact owner email.

entries.title: 60-day friend invites and onboarding emails
entries.summary: Invited friends get 60 days of unlimited core knowledge transfers from verified redemption, with a workspace countdown and an extension link. Adds an onboarding email series and optional Jev processing.

entries.title: Email-only console sign-in
entries.summary: Hosted sign-in and invite screens use email verification only. Agent access tokens can no longer open a console session, though agents still use them.

entries.title: Invite screen copy
entries.summary: The invite screen now reads: “No card required. Verify your email to get started.”

entries.title: Invite-only hosted beta
entries.summary: Hosted sign-up requires a single-use invitation bound to the recipient's email, plus inbox verification.

entries.title: Hosted launch
entries.summary: The hosted service launches with workspace-scoped credentials, isolated workers, billing, privacy and support pages, and an activity view that separates observed memory calls from tasks agents report. Guided onboarding advances as setup succeeds.

entries.title: A helpful page at /mcp
entries.summary: Opening the MCP URL in a browser explains how to paste it into a ChatGPT, Claude or Grok connector instead of showing a blank error.

entries.title: Sign in from chat connectors
entries.summary: Engram runs its own OAuth authorization server. Claude, ChatGPT and Grok connectors sign in with the same email link as the console.

entries.title: Share slices from a personal brain
entries.summary: Notes land in a personal brain first. Share rules copy matching slices into a team brain, and a share can be undone.

entries.title: README as the project front page
entries.summary: The README explains what Engram is, how to self-host it and how to ask for hosted access.

entries.title: Keep Jev on across deploys
entries.summary: Deploys keep the Jev provider key mounted, so a routine release cannot switch Jev off.

entries.title: Restore proven deploy settings
entries.summary: Deployment returns to the last working Cloud Run configuration so the Jev release could go live.

entries.title: Deploy before provider access is ready
entries.summary: Deploys skip provider keys until access is granted. Jev stays off and memory keeps working.

entries.title: Optional provider keys
entries.summary: Releases mount the Jev and embedding keys only when they exist; otherwise the gateway runs without them.

entries.title: Run the Jev tests in the build
entries.summary: Tests preload the database setting they need, so the Jev suite runs in Cloud Build.

entries.title: Fix the provider key build step
entries.summary: The build escapes its shell variables so it can create provider key placeholders.

entries.title: Jev memory cycle and nightly consolidation
entries.summary: Optional Jev judgments route topics, classify notes and rerank recall, and a nightly job consolidates memory. Saves still work when Jev is down.

entries.title: Graph view, live usage and provenance
entries.summary: The console shows which agent first wrote a page and who has added to it since, a graph of pages and their links, and live usage.

entries.title: Console redesign
entries.summary: The console drops its paper-and-ink theme and Japanese vocabulary for a plainer design and plain terms.

entries.title: Record which page each call touched
entries.summary: Each call records the page it touched: the groundwork for showing where a memory came from and who contributed to it.

entries.title: Long topic pages stay current
entries.summary: Topic pages are bounded and roll over, instead of recall cutting the answer off mid-sentence and returning an old state.

entries.title: Fix the deploy trigger
entries.summary: The automatic deploy names a log destination, so the trigger can run.

entries.title: Notes on a hidden test bug
entries.summary: Adds notes on how a global test mock removed exports and why a local container run hid the problem.

entries.title: Test mocks keep real exports
entries.summary: Module mocks keep the exports they do not replace, fixing the first automated build failure.

entries.title: Deploy on merge, gated on tests
entries.summary: Merging to main deploys automatically, and only after the test suite passes.

entries.title: No failed connection after idle
entries.summary: An idle Engram no longer fails an agent's first connection while it wakes up.

entries.title: No lost saves from concurrent writers
entries.summary: Concurrent saves to the same page verify what they wrote, so one agent's entry is not dropped by another's.

entries.title: Headless agent permissions guide
entries.summary: Documents the tool permissions headless agents need to reach Engram, and scopes the OAuth work.

entries.title: Saves to one page run in order
entries.summary: Saves to the same page run one at a time, so two agents appending together no longer drop an entry. Tool counts in the docs were corrected.

entries.title: remember and recall
entries.summary: Adds the remember and recall tools, short tool descriptions, response size caps and MCP server instructions.

entries.title: Bridge setup from npm
entries.summary: The wiring guide drops its clone-and-run workaround now that the bridge is published on npm.

entries.title: Bridge command path
entries.summary: Fixes the bridge's command path so the published package matches the repository.

entries.title: Bridge package links
entries.summary: The npm package links to the correct repository, homepage and issue tracker.

entries.title: Ready for other people to run
entries.summary: Removes an unused cloud dependency, corrects the package description and adds CI that runs the tests on every change.

entries.title: One brain
entries.summary: Engram collapses to a single brain with one tool surface, and forgetting a page can be undone.

entries.title: A browser console
entries.summary: Adds a browser console to search, browse, read and quickly capture memory. The gateway serves it with no build step.

entries.title: MIT license and stateless MCP
entries.summary: Engram is MIT licensed and supports the 2026-07-28 stateless MCP specification.

entries.title: Engram v0
entries.summary: A scoped MCP gateway over gbrain, with per-agent tokens and a separate database for each scope.

entries.title: First commit
entries.summary: The first gateway: MCP over HTTP with per-agent bearer tokens, an audit log, an admin CLI and a docker-compose self-host path.
